source.title: From Local to Global to Mechanistic: An iERF-Centered Unified Framework for Interpreting Vision Models
source.authors: Yearim Kim; Sang-Yu Han; N. Kwak

record.file_problem: Minor PDF-extraction artifacts in equations and formatting; the full paper is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper mentions superposition as motivation and studies SAE features in vision models, but does not test whether sparse features compete for limited dimensions or what geometry they take.
record.gate_note: The paper's superposition and polysemanticity statements are background motivation, not results. Its SAE experiments concern visual concept interpretation and attribution, not superposition capacity or feature geometry. The qualitative observations of dispersed SAE activations in vision models are recorded as related findings, not as evidence for the LLM-specific versions.
record.test_reason: Superposition and polysemanticity appear only as background motivation for the PFV unit (Sec. III-A). The SAE work concerns grounding vision-transformer SAE latents in pixel attributions (CAFE) and choosing a concept extractor for a mechanistic graph. No result bears on capacity, feature geometry, sparsity transitions, causes of polysemanticity, feature dimensionality, or whether SAE features are canonical. The studied systems are vision models, not LLMs.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors present a unified iERF-based framework (SRD, CAFE, ICAT) for vision models. They state that CAFE recovers feature activations faster in insertion tests. They also state that non-localized SAE features are rare in early layers and more common in deeper Transformer blocks. They frame the framework as an attribution-based proxy, not formal causal identification.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not reproduce or apply the Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that non-localized SAE phenomena are rare in early layers and more common in later Transformer layers.

fits_no_version.finding: In CLIP-ViT-L/14, some SAE latents activate across distant image regions. The top-activating token can sit on an incidental location. Per the authors, non-locality is rare in early layers and more common in later ones.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Vision-transformer SAE latents can be spatially non-localized, with prevalence rising with depth; attribution (iERF) identifies their input evidence better than activation ranking.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: The examples of non-localized SAE features are qualitative and limited; the paper does not report a quantitative prevalence estimate for this phenomenon.
record.rows_left_out: The SAE-versus-dictionary-learning-versus-k-means reconstruction and sparsity comparisons in Table III, and the CAFE insertion tests in Fig. 7, evaluate concept extraction or attribution rather than the capacity, geometry, dimensionality, or canonical status named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: No toy models, no capacity or sparsity-transition analysis, no feature geometry.
No test of whether polysemanticity arises from competition for capacity.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
SAEs are trained on CLIP-ViT-L/14 only; no LLM results on distributed features or SAE recovery.

The SAE-vs-k-means comparison (Tab. III, Fig. 15) and the cited SAE instability (Archetypal SAE) are extractor choices for a vision pipeline. They are not tests of completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features.
Concepts are assumed to be linear directions; dimensionality is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: Rows r1–r5 are qualitative single-feature examples, and their 'none' links are correct. Tab. III reports SAE reconstruction error, with SAE denser and higher in error than k-means in intermediate ResNet layers. Some SAE Rel-l2 values exceed 1, which looks odd. That comparison bears on extractor quality for this pipeline, not on any version, so leaving it out is reasonable. Toy Models of Superposition is cited only as background.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network feature capacity, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry are not tested.
The study does not test whether polysemantic neurons result from features competing for capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
The study does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
The studied systems are vision models, not LLMs; the paper does not test LLM feature distribution across neurons or SAE recovery.
The study does not establish whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of a model's representation.
The study does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: CLIP–ViT-L/14
rows.operation_detail: Qualitative inspection of SAE latent activation locations across top-activated samples.
rows.value: Activation is spatially dispersed across multiple distant regions; the most activated token can fall on an incidental location.
rows.note: Vision-model SAE example; the paper uses it to motivate attribution-based grounding rather than to test superposition.
